attempts.raw_response: "But I do think there needs to be more creative thinking about how we deliver services. It's not just about cutting back; it's about working smarter." He pointed to examples of councils sharing resources and digitising services as potential ways to bridge funding gaps. When asked about the timeline for these changes, Mr Faulkner warned that residents could start seeing the impact within the next two to three years if central government didn't intervene. "The reality is, something has to give. Either we get more funding or we get realistic about what a council can provide," he added, urging ministers to engage with local government leaders before the situation deteriorated further.
